lines.text: Saw three cutters past the breakwater. Ain't none of 'em flying colors.
lines.context: Reporting suspicious ship activity to an ally

lines.text: Don't look at me like that. Cargo's cargo.
lines.context: Deflecting moral judgment about what he transports

lines.text: Tide don't wait. Neither do I.
lines.context: Pressing someone to make a decision quickly

lines.text: Had a partner once. Good man. Anchor chain.
lines.context: Alluding to a dead partner without elaborating

lines.text: Keep your voice down. Walls got barnacles with ears.
lines.context: Warning an ally they might be overheard

lines.text: Paid 'em last Tuesday. Whole crate, salt-sealed, smelled like rust and pine.
lines.context: Lying about a delivery — over-explaining sensory details

lines.text: Get out.
lines.context: Discovering someone searched his quarters

lines.text: Say that again. Slower.
lines.context: Threatening someone who insulted him

lines.text: Touch the wheel. Lose the hand.
lines.context: Warning someone off his boat controls

lines.text: Done talking. Move.
lines.context: Ending a negotiation that went wrong

lines.text: Burned my license. Burned my dock. Still here, ain't I?
lines.context: Confronting the authority that ruined him

lines.text: Oughta throw y'all overboard and call it weather.
lines.context: Threatening stowaways found in his cargo hold

lines.text: Oh sure, let's ask the harbor master. He's real helpful with smugglers.
lines.context: Mocking a naive suggestion to go through official channels

lines.text: Real pretty plan. Y'all want matching life vests too?
lines.context: Dismissing an overly optimistic heist plan

lines.text: Ain't my first squall. Won't be my last neither.
lines.context: Downplaying danger to appear unfazed

lines.text: Got a boat, got fuel, got 'nuff ammo. What I ain't got is a reason to trust you.
lines.context: Listing assets before the punchline refusal

lines.text: Captain's log: still surrounded by idiots.
lines.context: Muttering after a team blunder

lines.text: Need to get past the blockade — tonight. Got no other channel.
lines.context: Begging an old contact to smuggle him through a naval cordon

lines.text: Fuel's gone — hull's cracked — we drift or we sink, pick one.
lines.context: Ship breaking apart, forcing an impossible choice

lines.text: Tell 'em I'll run anything. Anything. Just need the boat back.
lines.context: Agreeing to a dangerous job to recover his seized vessel

lines.text: Can't lose another one. Not out here. Not like this.
lines.context: Watching a crewmate bleed out during a storm

lines.text: 'Oh, the sea is my calling.' Yeah. Called me a fool and took everything.
lines.context: Mocking a romantic's idea of the sailor's life

lines.text: 'Strategic maritime asset.' That what y'all calling a leaky dinghy now?
lines.context: Ridiculing military jargon from an official briefing

lines.text: 'Honor among thieves.' Cute. Show me the thief with honor and I'll show you a corpse.
lines.context: Dismissing a rival's appeal to loyalty

lines.text: 'Trust the process.' Love that. Real comforting when the process is on fire.
lines.context: Mocking a planner whose scheme is falling apart

lines.text: Two guards. Twelve-minute rotation. East dock blind spot at quarter past.
lines.context: Laying out a dock infiltration plan

lines.text: Current runs north after sundown. We ride it, save half the fuel.
lines.context: Planning a fuel-efficient escape route by sea

lines.text: Three exits. Two guarded. One underwater. Guess which one's ours.
lines.context: Briefing the team on a warehouse raid

lines.text: Shouldn't have come back. Know that now.
lines.context: Returning to the port where his partner died

lines.text: She was the only mooring I had. Rest is just drift.
lines.context: Speaking about someone he lost, late at night, guard down
